title: Change-of-Control Clause
summary: A contract between the target and a third party may require the third party's consent, permit termination, or trigger another remedy when ownership or control of the target changes. Unmanaged, these provisions can delay completion, increase costs, or result in the loss of critical contracts, revenue, and financing post-acquisition.

key_questions.question: Has the target company signed a contract with a third party containing a change-of-control, assignment, termination or analogous provision?
Does the proposed transaction trigger the change-of-control clause?
What are the consequences of the triggered provision?
How critical is this contract to the target’s business operations and valuation?
What is the likelihood, timing and any cost of obtaining consent or a waiver?

title: Termination Rights and Material Breaches
summary: The target may have important contracts affected by breaches or termination rights, such as major customer, critical supply, distribution or key licence agreements. Review actual or suspected breaches, the counterparty’s right to end the contract, and steps to preserve the relationship or manage its loss before completion.

key_questions.question: Has a breach or termination risk been identified under a material contract?
What does the issue concern?
What stage has the matter reached?
What is the likely impact on the target or deal?
Can the issue and its consequences be addressed before completion?

title: Option Holders
summary: The target may have outstanding options, warrants or similar rights that affect the fully diluted ownership position and the mechanics of a sale. The transaction must identify every relevant award and implement its treatment so that the buyer receives the agreed capital structure at completion.

key_questions.question: Are there any outstanding options, warrants or other rights to acquire shares?
Does the award register reconcile with the fully diluted cap table and supporting documents?
How will the outstanding awards be treated in the transaction? (select all that apply)
Can the proposed treatment be validly implemented by completion?
What proportion of the fully diluted share capital is represented by the outstanding awards?
What is the tax and payroll position for the proposed treatment?

title: Share Ownership and Transfer Restrictions
summary: Unverified ownership, unwilling sellers, transfer restrictions or security over the shares can delay completion or prevent the buyer from acquiring the agreed shares.

key_questions.question: Do all sellers have verified ownership of their sale shares?
Have all shareholders needed for the acquisition agreed to sell?
Are there any restrictions on transferring the sale shares?
Have all transfer restrictions been addressed?
Is there any security over the sale shares?
Will the security be released at completion?

title: Debt Facilities Requiring Repayment
summary: The target may have borrowing facilities that become repayable, require lender consent or otherwise need to be addressed because of the proposed transaction. A failure to repay or release security at completion can leave debt, guarantees or encumbrances affecting the acquired business.

key_questions.question: Does any target-group company have outstanding borrowing, guarantees or security under a finance arrangement?
What does the proposed transaction require under the finance documents?
Has the lender confirmed the full repayment amount and release conditions in writing?
Has the required lender consent or waiver been obtained in writing?
Are sufficient funds available under an agreed completion funds flow?
Are all target-group security, guarantees and other credit support identified, with releases agreed for completion?
Are all required lender steps sequenced with completion?

notes:
Transaction triggers: Check the precise change-of-control, mandatory prepayment, cancellation and default wording against the agreed transaction structure; repayment alone may not address every consent or notice requirement.

Register updates: Check the required post-completion filings separately from the contractual release. A Companies House MR04 records satisfaction on the public register; filing it does not remove the charge entry.

title: Missing IP Assignment
summary: A founder, employee, contractor, group company or other third party may have created IP used by the target without an effective transfer of ownership to the target. This can impair the target's ability to use, license, enforce or transfer the relevant IP.

key_questions.question: Is there a potentially missing IP assignment?
Does the target have complete, executed and enforceable documents evidencing ownership or a sufficient right to use the IP?
How important is the affected IP to the target's operations and value?
How difficult would it be to rewrite or redesign the affected asset from scratch?
What is the relationship between the target and the current IP owner? i.e. the current IP owner is in relation to the target…
Has the IP owner ever asserted an ownership claim, royalty demand, or threat of litigation?

title: Threatened Litigation
summary: A third party may have threatened, or there may be a credible prospect of, a claim against the target. Even before proceedings are issued, the matter can create financial, operational, reputational and completion risk and may require specific diligence and contractual protection.

key_questions.question: Has the target received, or is it aware of, a credible threat of legal action?
What stage has the matter reached and are the relevant procedural deadlines understood?
Has the claim and the target's available defences been assessed?
What is the likely impact on the target and the transaction?
Is the target's exposure reduced by insurance, indemnities, limitations or contribution rights?
Can the matter be fully and durably resolved before completion?

recommended_actions.recommendation: Review the claim’s factual basis, procedural status, merits, potential exposure and likely effect on the target and transaction.
recommended_actions.rationale: The parties need a reliable understanding of the claim before settling the transaction terms.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Obtain or update privileged legal advice on the claim, available defences, likely remedies and a reasonable settlement range.
recommended_actions.rationale: A legally informed assessment is important where the merits or exposure are uncertain.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Agree specific disclosure of the claim, exposure, recovery position and material developments, while protecting privilege.
recommended_actions.rationale: Specific disclosure establishes the known position against which transaction protections can be negotiated.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Confirm available insurance and other recovery rights, and satisfy applicable notice, consent and preservation requirements.
recommended_actions.rationale: Available recoveries may materially reduce the target's net exposure if they remain enforceable and properly preserved.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Agree and implement a binding resolution before completion, including any remaining payments, releases and procedural steps.
recommended_actions.rationale: A binding resolution can remove or materially reduce the identified transaction risk.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Agree objective litigation milestones as completion conditions, with a longstop date and proportionate waiver and termination rights.
recommended_actions.rationale: A completion condition may be appropriate where the buyer should not assume an unresolved material risk.

recommended_actions.recommendation: If signing precedes completion, agree controls over material admissions, settlements and strategy changes, allowing timely compliance with procedural duties.
recommended_actions.rationale: Interim controls prevent the target's position from being materially altered before completion.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Agree appropriately qualified warranties covering the dispute position, related undisclosed claims and material developments, supported by specific disclosure.
recommended_actions.rationale: Targeted warranties support the accuracy and completeness of the contractual risk record.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Agree a specific indemnity for defined litigation losses, with clear limits, claims control and treatment of recoveries.
recommended_actions.rationale: A specific indemnity can allocate the financial consequences of a known, unresolved claim.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Agree proportionate escrow or retention for identified litigation exposure, with clear payment and release triggers.
recommended_actions.rationale: Ring-fenced consideration provides security for an unresolved exposure.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Agree any price adjustment for material litigation exposure, taking account of expected losses, costs and recoveries without double counting.
recommended_actions.rationale: A direct price adjustment may be appropriate where the exposure affects the agreed valuation.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Agree any litigation reserve or completion accounts adjustment, with clear accounting policies and no duplicate recovery.
recommended_actions.rationale: The completion mechanism can reflect a measurable exposure without duplicating other protections.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Check W&I exclusions for the known dispute and explore available cover for related exposures without assuming the dispute is insured.
recommended_actions.rationale: Early engagement can clarify whether any related exposure is capable of insurance protection.

recommended_actions.recommendation: Consider termination rights for defined material litigation developments, with objective thresholds and agreed exclusions.
recommended_actions.rationale: A specific walk-right can protect the buyer against serious deterioration before completion.

title: Key Employee Retention and Employment Terms
summary: The target may depend on employees whose departure would affect its operations or value. Review their plans, employment terms and transaction payments to identify any retention or handover arrangements needed for continuity.

key_questions.question: Does the target depend on particular employees for its operations or value?
How difficult would it be to replace those employees without disrupting the business?
Do those employees intend to remain with the target after completion?
Do their employment terms allow enough time for replacement and handover?
Will the transaction trigger bonuses, severance or other employee payments?
Are any necessary retention or handover arrangements agreed?

title: Compliance Gaps and Personal Data Breaches
summary: The target may have compliance gaps or personal data breaches affecting how it collects, uses or protects personal data. Review the issues, potential exposure and remedial steps to identify any effect on the transaction and work needed before completion.

key_questions.question: Has a data protection issue been identified?
What does the issue concern?
Is the issue still ongoing?
Have required breach notifications been made?
Are there related complaints, claims or regulatory enquiries? (select all that apply)
What is the likely impact on the target or deal?
Can all necessary remedial steps be completed before completion?
